intro.heading: Finding the words that aren't there
intro.body:
You'll read three shift notes. Tap every word or phrase a camera couldn't have recorded.

A camera records what it sees and hears. It can't record a mood, a motive, or a reason.

No time limit, and no penalty for trying again.

notes.label: Note 1
notes.text: Assisted Mary with her shopping. She was *in a good mood* and *clearly enjoyed* being out. Mary chose her own items and paid at the self-checkout without help. *Seemed much happier* than last week.

feedback.in a good mood: A conclusion. What did Mary do that gave you that impression? Write that instead.
feedback.clearly enjoyed: "Clearly" is doing a lot of work here. It's your read, not a recording.
feedback.Seemed much happier: Compared to what, and measured how? This is the kind of line that follows someone around their file.

trapFeedback.chose: This one's fine. A camera sees someone choosing items off a shelf.
trapFeedback.paid: Fine — and specific. It tells the next worker she handled the checkout herself.
trapFeedback.self-checkout: Keep it. It's exactly the detail that shows what she can do.

notes.label: Note 2
notes.text: David was *uncooperative* this morning. *His autism makes transitions difficult*, so he *refused* breakfast and stayed in his room for 20 minutes. *Eventually* came out and ate half a slice of toast. *Attitude improved* by the end of the shift.

feedback.uncooperative: This describes your experience of David, not David's behaviour. "Stayed in his room for 20 minutes" is already there and does the job.
feedback.His autism makes transitions difficult: Two problems. It states a cause you didn't witness, and the label means something different to every worker who reads it. What David actually did is already in the next clause.
feedback.refused: Arguable, and that's why the pass mark isn't 100%. It describes an action but imports an intention. "Did not eat breakfast" asserts less.
feedback.Eventually: Carries a sigh. How long was it? You already know: twenty minutes.
feedback.Attitude improved: Improved how? A camera would have recorded him coming out and eating. Write that.

trapFeedback.20: Keep it. A number is the most useful thing in this note.
trapFeedback.minutes: Keep it. A number is the most useful thing in this note.
trapFeedback.toast: Fine. Specific, countable, and it tells the next worker he ate something.

notes.label: Note 3
notes.text: Took John to his appointment. He was *anxious* in the car, tapping his hands on his knees the whole way. Waited 40 minutes. John told me he did not want to go back.

feedback.anxious: The only one in this note. And look what's sitting right next to it — you already wrote the observation.

trapFeedback.tapping: This one's fine. A camera records tapping hands. This is the observation that supports "anxious" — keep it, and drop the label.
trapFeedback.hands: This one's fine. A camera records tapping hands. This is the observation that supports "anxious" — keep it, and drop the label.
trapFeedback.knees: This one's fine. A camera records tapping hands. This is the observation that supports "anxious" — keep it, and drop the label.
trapFeedback.told: Keep it. He said it; you heard it. Reported speech is recordable.
trapFeedback.want: Keep it. That's what John told you, not what you concluded.

results.pass: That's the skill. You're finding the places where a conclusion slipped in — which is exactly what you'll be doing to your own notes from now on.
results.fail: Have another go. The question for every word is the same one: could a camera have recorded this?
results.perfect: All of them, and you left the observations alone. That second part is the harder half.
